subject: Clarify: transient PHI in streaming transcription + BAA / evidence
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medscribe.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@healthops.org>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: PHI handling for live transcription stream — BAA + evidence request

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking a look. We're kicking off an evaluation of Redwood for a live patient-call transcription feature. A few quick things we need to confirm before we proceed:

1) Transient PHI in streaming: When using Redwood's streaming transcription endpoint, will any PHI tokens (patient names, MRNs, SSNs, or other identifiers) be written to persistent logs, KV caches, or metric traces by default? If so, what fields are persisted and for how long (audit logs, raw audio, transcript chunks, token-level logs)?

2) "No-persistence" mode: Do you support a configuration where transcripts and intermediate tokens are never written to persistent storage (i.e., kept only in RAM until returned to our client and then immediately dropped)? If so, please describe the deployment modes where this is available (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

3) Evidence: We need SOC2 Type II, CAIQ/SIG artifacts, and a signed BAA to satisfy our internal and partner compliance teams. Can you attach the latest SOC2 report and confirm whether you support customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest? Also, do you support IP allowlisting and per-tenant access logs?

4) Retention SLA: Our default needs are 7 days max for transcripts, and 0 days for intermediate caches. Can Redwood commit to configurable retention windows and a verifiable deletion API?

We're trying to get a BAA executed and evidence into our vendor security questionnaire by next week. Copying Raj from HealthOps (our compliance lead) for visibility.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Product, MedScribeAI

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (Security Ops) and Soojin (Product Security) to confirm details below and to own the BAA/evidence handoff. High level answers first, then specifics:

- Short answer: We can support a "no-persistence" streaming mode, but availability and guarantees depend on deployment (hosted vs dedicated/private) and the SLAs you need. Dedicated and Private both support stronger isolation and no-persistence configs.

Detailed:
1) Default persistence (hosted): by default our hosted streaming endpoints emit transcript chunks to the response stream and write request/response metadata to short-term logs and metrics for observability and billing. Default retention for request logs is 30 days. Transcript artifacts in hosted are not persisted beyond the retention window unless you enable long-term storage.

- What may be written (hosted default): request metadata (timestamp, route, model id), streaming chunk IDs (opaque), and short-lived transcript shards used for debugging. We do not persist raw audio in hosted unless you opt in (e.g., for recording features).

2) No-persistence mode:
- Dedicated: supports a configuration flag to disable transcript persistence and disable token-level telemetry; KV caches are kept in-memory and not persisted to disk. We can also disable any metrics that include transcript snippets.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): you control all storage and can configure true RAM-only handling at the infra layer; we can provide a deployment manifest describing the memory-only flow for your infra team.

3) KMS / encryption / allowlist / logs:
- Customer-managed KMS: supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted customers currently use our managed KMS but we offer envelope encryption and can discuss bring-your-own-key for enterprise contracts.
- IP allowlisting / egress restrictions: supported via our networking controls for Dedicated and Private.
- Access/audit logs: we provide audit event streams; retention is configurable on Dedicated/Private and can be integrated with your SIEM.

4) Retention/deletion API:
- We provide a deletion API and programmatic retention config for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we offer shorter retention defaults and an enterprise deletion SLA.

Next steps: Monica / Soojin — can you confirm the exact artifacts we can attach here for Elena (SOC2, SIG/CAIQ, encryption statements) and whether we can provide a DocuSign BAA link? Also Elena, it would help to know targeted RPS and whether you need streaming partial-results to be returned to client before Redwood confirms deletion (i.e., client-side ephemeral token exchange vs server-side).

I'll attach the SOC2 PDF and a DocuSign BAA link in a follow-up.

Thanks,
Mateo
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi all — thanks Mateo, that helps. A few clarifications from our side:

- Throughput: expected peak for proof-of-concept is ~25 concurrent streams, ramping to ~200 over 3 months. Average call length ~6 minutes.
- We need a documented "no-persistence" guarantee for hosted evaluation (proof-of-concept) — our security team will accept a signed attestation that transcripts and intermediate tokens are not persisted beyond RAM for the duration of the POC. Is Redwood able to provide that for a timeboxed POC on your hosted environment?
- For production, we are strongly leaning to Dedicated (for per-tenant KMS and IP allowlist).
- Evidence: can you also provide a completed CAIQ spreadsheet and a redacted SIG? Raj will import these to our vendor portal.

If you can send a DocuSign BAA link and the CAIQ/SIG artifacts today, we can get the internal review started. Also please confirm whether any model telemetry (e.g., anonymized failure samples or quality telemetry) could contain verbatim PHI and whether that telemetry can be disabled.

Best,
Elena
